### Subject: Opinion on Indian tax implications of an offshore transfer of shares deriving value from Indian assets

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Falcon Capital Partners (Mauritius), and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. ## 2. Statement of Facts

Falcon Mauritius Holdco's sole asset is its shareholding in an Indian operating company, from which it derives more than 50% of its total value, well above the INR 10 crore threshold. Its Cayman Islands parent proposes to sell 100% of Falcon Mauritius Holdco to an unrelated buyer.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the proposed offshore share transfer triggers Indian capital gains tax under the indirect transfer provisions of Section 9(1)(i), Explanation 5.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 9(1)(i), Explanation 5
- Rule 11UB


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Vodafone International Holdings BV v. UOI, (2012) 341 ITR 1 (SC)
- Tiger Global International II Holdings v. AAR (Del HC, 2020)

## 6. Analysis

Since the Indian assets constitute a majority of Falcon Mauritius Holdco's value and exceed the prescribed threshold, and the Cayman parent's 100% holding is well above the 5% de minimis exemption available to small shareholders not in management or control, the transfer falls squarely within Explanation 5. Capital gains attributable to the Indian assets, computed per the methodology under Rule 11UB, would accordingly be taxable in India.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The transaction constitutes a taxable indirect transfer; the buyer would be required to withhold tax under Section 195 on the India-attributable portion of the gains.

**Confidence level:** High
